newsitem.title: USA: KCBT wheat sets 10-month high on freeze, floods.
newsitem.headline: KCBT wheat sets 10-month high on freeze, floods.

text.p: KCBT hard red winter wheat futures set a 10-month high on concerns about harsh weather in several key global wheat producing regions, traders said.
"More of the same. It's been very choppy and we're in kind of a lull now and we've been rallying into the close so the close will be interesting," a trader said.

Flooding in the northern U.S. spring wheat growing region, persistent reports of crop losses from a recent freeze in the U.S. Great Plains hard red winter wheat region and apparent worsening drought conditions in key European wheat growing areas, led the advances.
Nearby May set a fresh 10-month high of $5.14 per bushel just below the $5.17 set on June 18, 1996. The contract high for May is $5.75 and was set May 8, 1996.
The new contract high for September is $4.98, well above the previous high of $4.81 set Friday.
At 1155 CDT, KCBT wheat was 7-1/2 to 13 cents per bushel higher, with May up eight at $5.08 a bushel and July was up 7-1/2 at $4.88-1/2.
